title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant J (Family, friends and celebrations)

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions:
Part 1.1 - Family, friends and celebrations - Level A1-A2 - Scored items 1, 2 and 3.
You will be asked three short questions about yourself and the people around you. The questions are asked one after another. There is NO preparation time. You have 30 seconds to answer each question. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.
Examiner: items 1-3 are marked together on a scale of 0-5.

questions.q:
PART 1.1 - CEFR MULTILEVEL SPEAKING - VARIANT J - THEME: FAMILY, FRIENDS AND CELEBRATIONS
Level A1-A2. Scored items 1-3 (marked together, 0-5).

[STAGE DIRECTION: no preparation time. Ask the three questions one after another. Play the chime, then start a 30-second timer for each answer. At 30 seconds say "Thank you" and move straight on to the next question. Do not explain vocabulary, and do not repeat a question more than once.]

EXAMINER - READ ALOUD EXACTLY:
"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 1 - 30 SECONDS
(chime)
"How many people live in your home, and who are they?"
[Timer: 30 seconds. At the end: "Thank you."]

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 2 - 30 SECONDS
(chime)
"Which member of your family do you talk to most often, and what do you talk about?"
[Timer: 30 seconds. At the end: "Thank you."]

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 3 - 30 SECONDS
(chime)
"What do you usually do on your birthday?"
[Timer: 30 seconds. At the end: "Thank you."]

[STAGE DIRECTION: Part 1.1 and Part 1.2 together make up Part one, so do not announce an ending here. Put the two photographs in front of the candidate and go straight on to Part 1.2.]

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions:
Part 1.2 - Family, friends and celebrations - Level B1 - Scored items 4, 5 and 6.
You will see two photographs on one theme. You will be asked three questions, one after another. There is NO preparation time. Question 4 (comparing the two pictures) gives you 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 give you 30 seconds each. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.
Examiner: items 4-6 are marked together on a scale of 0-5.

questions.q:
PART 1.2 - CEFR MULTILEVEL SPEAKING - VARIANT J - THEME: FAMILY, FRIENDS AND CELEBRATIONS
Level B1. Scored items 4-6 (marked together, 0-5).

[STAGE DIRECTION: no preparation time. Place the two photographs in front of the candidate side by side. If no printed photographs are available, read the two descriptions below aloud, slowly, before asking question 4. Question 4 = 45 seconds. Questions 5 and 6 = 30 seconds each.]

THE TWO PHOTOGRAPHS:
[PICTURE 1: a large outdoor wedding celebration in a courtyard at dusk - about sixty guests seated at long tables covered with white cloths, strings of small lights hanging overhead, a band with a drum and a clarinet playing at the far end, several children running between the tables, waiters carrying wide trays of food, and the bride and groom standing up to greet an elderly couple.]
[PICTURE 2: a small birthday at home - a grandmother and one grandchild sitting at a kitchen table in the afternoon, a single home-made cake with four candles between them, two cups of tea, a simple paper banner taped to a cupboard door, afternoon light through the window, and nobody else in the room.]

EXAMINER - READ ALOUD EXACTLY:
"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs."
[STAGE DIRECTION: the final sentence of the official wording, "What do you see in these pictures?", is scored item 4 below. Read it once only, then start the 45-second timer.]

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 4 - 45 SECONDS (the compare and describe question)
(chime)
"What do you see in these pictures?"
[Prompt only if the candidate stops very early: "How are the two celebrations different?"]
[Timer: 45 seconds. At the end: "Thank you."]

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 5 - 30 SECONDS (opinion)
(chime)
"Which of these two celebrations would you prefer to be invited to, and why?"
[Timer: 30 seconds. At the end: "Thank you."]

----------------------------------------
SCORED ITEM 6 - 30 SECONDS (opinion)
(chime)
"Some people say a celebration is only successful if a great many guests come. Do you agree? Why, or why not?"
[Timer: 30 seconds. At the end: "Thank you. That is the end of Part one."]

[STAGE DIRECTION: take the photographs away and move on to Part two.]

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions:
Part 2 - Family traditions across the generations - Level B2 - Scored item 7.
You will see one picture and be asked three questions, all at the same time. You are NOT required to describe the picture; it is there only to introduce the topic. You have 1 minute to think about your answers and then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.
Examiner: item 7 is marked on a scale of 0-5.

questions.q:
PART 2 - CEFR MULTILEVEL SPEAKING - VARIANT J - THEME: FAMILY TRADITIONS ACROSS THE GENERATIONS
Level B2. Scored item 7 (0-5).

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the picture and present all three questions together, on the screen or read aloud, before the preparation minute begins. Give exactly 1 minute of silent preparation; the candidate may make notes. Then play the chime and time 2 minutes for all three answers together. Do not interrupt during the two minutes. The candidate is NOT required to describe the picture - say so if the candidate asks.]

THE PICTURE:
[PICTURE: three generations of one family cooking together in a bright kitchen - an elderly woman in an apron shaping dough at a floured table, her adult daughter beside her filling a large dish, and a boy of about ten standing on a low stool stirring a bowl and watching closely; a worn recipe notebook covered in handwriting lies open on the windowsill, and a phone propped against a jar is filming them.]

EXAMINER - READ ALOUD EXACTLY:
"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

"You do not have to describe the picture. Here are your three questions."

THE THREE QUESTIONS (presented together):
1. Tell me about a family tradition or celebration that you have taken part in.
2. How has taking part in it affected your relationship with your relatives?
3. What factors most influence whether families today keep their traditions alive or let them disappear?

[STAGE DIRECTION: "You have one minute to prepare. Your time starts now." - time 1 minute in silence.]
[STAGE DIRECTION: after one minute - "Please begin." (chime) - time 2 minutes for all three questions together. At 2 minutes: "Thank you. That is the end of Part two."]

questions.q:
PART 3 - CEFR MULTILEVEL SPEAKING - VARIANT J - THEME: THE COST OF FAMILY CELEBRATIONS
Level C1. Scored item 8 (0-6).

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the topic statement and both lists on the screen, or write them out and place them in front of the candidate. Give exactly 1 minute of silent preparation, then play the chime and time 2 minutes. Do not interrupt. The candidate must choose TWO points from the FOR list and TWO points from the AGAINST list and build a balanced argument; a personal conclusion is permitted but not required.]

EXAMINER - READ ALOUD EXACTLY:
"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

========================================
TOPIC STATEMENT:
"Families should spend far less money on weddings and other large celebrations."
========================================

FOR - spend less
1. Young couples often begin married life in debt because of a single day.
2. The same money could pay for a home, for study, or for a family business.
3. Competition between families puts unfair pressure on those who can afford it least.

AGAINST - the spending is justified
1. Large gatherings renew ties between relatives who rarely meet.
2. Costly celebrations keep customs, music and food traditions alive.
3. The money circulates locally, supporting cooks, musicians, tailors and hall owners.
========================================

[STAGE DIRECTION: "You have one minute to prepare. Your time starts now." - time 1 minute in silence.]
[STAGE DIRECTION: after one minute - "Please begin." (chime) - time 2 minutes. At 2 minutes: "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]
